newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rice prices up on Syria, S.Africa demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian rice prices up on Syria, S.Africa demand.

text.p: Indian rice export prices rose marginally during the week due to firm demand from Syria and South Africa, traders said on Thursday.

"Prices have risen somewhat because of good demand from Syria and South African destinations," Prem Garg, managing director of Shivnath Rai Harnarayan, a leading Delhi foodgrains exporter, told Reuters.
Traders said Indian five percent broken non-Basmati rice was quoted at $315 per tonne FOB, 10 percent at $300, 15 percent at $260-$270 and 25 percent at $250 per tonne.
Exporters said they had contracted for 50,000 tonnes of rice exports during the week.

"The demand for lower grades of rice is more than higher grades as higher grades prices are not competitive compared with Vietnam and Pakistan," Rashmi Bhimjayani, a leading Bombay foodgrains exporter, said.
Traders said export prices of Indian five percent broken non-Basmati rice was about $20 per tonne more compared with that of Vietnam and Pakistan.
"Therefore we are not able to make much of headway in rice exports," Bhimjayani said. "We are only competitive in the 100 percent broken variety."
Traders said Indian 100 percent broken grade non-Basmati for exports was quoted at $180 to $185 per tonne and the demand was mainly from African countries.
"There is good demand for Indian Basmati rice from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Western Europe," Bhimjayani said.
Traders said Indian super variety Basmati rice was quoted at $1,000 per tonne FOB, against about $800 per tonne at the same time last year.
